clips.title: The story
paras: South of Lake Everstill, Underbelly Whelp Scale trades hands among Redridge craftsmen. Black dragon whelps provide the pliable scales, and local artisans value them when coin is scarce.

Black dragons bear tough scales, but facing a full-grown one is deadly for ordinary folk. South of Lake Everstill, black dragon whelps nest among the crags. Their back plates can be brittle or coarse, while the softer scales beneath their bellies bend more readily and still offer protection. Those qualities make Underbelly Whelp Scale valuable in local trade. Craftsmen prize it, and creditors can accept it in place of coin.

In Lakeshire, craftsmen sometimes barter when coin runs short or trade routes are strained. Verner Osgood, the local blacksmith, owes a heavy debt to Argus, a blacksmith in Goldshire. The debt began with a shipment of shoes brought in from Goldshire. Argus favors rare trade goods, so Verner depends on travelers to gather underbelly whelp scales. They can help settle what he owes and keep his workshop in good standing.
